This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Yemen Ansarallah strike on military camp in Yemen 's Shabwa kills 53, wounds at least 200: At least 53 soldiers were killed and over 200 injured in an Ansarallah targeting the Al-Alam military camp in the Shabwa governorate, according to the local government. Fighting is escalating across Yemen. Over the past 24 hours, the Ansarallah military spokesperson claimed Saudi forces carried out 110 airstrikes and missile attacks. Yemen's Saudi-backed government says its forces recaptured Sanamat and advanced toward Misrakh, south of Taiz city, following a counteroffensive against Ansarallah. Ansarallah forces have been besieging Taiz, where the UN has warned of dwindling food supplies. Saudi airstrike on house in Yemen kills at least 10, including five children: An airstrike on a family home in Yemen's Saada province blamed on Saudi-led forces killed at least 10 people on Sunday, including five children and three women, local media reported. Sana'a's National Human Rights Commission put the toll at 10 killed and 23 wounded, most of them women and children. shows men digging through the rubble with their hands. Saudi Arabia has not commented on the strike. Egypt seeks parliamentary approval for possible military intervention in support of Saudi Arabia: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi an urgent parliamentary session to authorize military support for Saudi Arabia, as Ansarallah attacks on the kingdom intensify, Reuters reports. A parliamentary vote was initially expected Sunday, but discussions are set to continue Monday and Tuesday. Egypt previously joined the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen in 2015 but played a limited combat role. Saudis and Emiratis meet amid reports UAE will resume support in Yemen: Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman met UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Abu Dhabi on Sunday. Bin Salman the two sides discussed "developments in the regional situation and ways to enhance cooperation and joint Gulf action." The meetings come amid that the UAE has agreed to resume funding anti-Ansarallah forces in Yemen, with Saudi Arabia providing air cover. U.S. warns Americans across Middle East of possible airspace closures: The United States issued security alerts on October 18 warning Americans across the Middle East of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and rapidly escalating hostilities.The warnings cover Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Kuwait, Jordan, Bahrain, Oman, Iran, Qatar, Iraq, Lebanon, Yemen, and Israel. The alerts also warned that Iran and groups aligned with Tehran could target U.S. interests abroad. Palestine UN food agency cuts Gaza aid for half a million Palestinians: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) major cuts in food assistance to Gaza cutting off half a million Palestinians from monthly food support, citing funding shortages. The agency is also halving food rations and reducing daily hot meals from 250,000 to 150,000. Those living in hard-to-reach areas, including near the Israeli military's yellow line, will receive hot meals every other day instead of daily. An estimated 67% of Gaza's population face acute food insecurity, including 200,000 experiencing emergency conditions requiring immediate assistance to prevent death from hunger. The cuts come as an Israeli blockade on commercial imports enters its fifth consecutive day, already causing a rise in the prices of basic goods, with sharp increases in the cost of flour, eggs, onions, and other staples. Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, five Palestinians were killed--four in new Israeli attacks and one due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks--and 22 injured across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Israel killed at least 12 Palestinians, including three children, and wounded 68 in attacks across the Strip over the weekend. An Israeli strike on Saturday killed 14-year-old Palestinian student Mohammed Abu Hammad in the south of Deir al-Balah in central Gaza shortly after he returned from school. "He hadn't even been sitting in the chair for five minutes," Ahmed Muhareb told Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed. "They fired a missile at the boy, while his schoolbag was still on his back." Watch the dispatch from Mohamed Ahmed The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023, is now 74,480 killed, with 175,539 injured. Since October 11, 2025, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,522 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 5,421, while 839 bodies have been recovered. Israeli forces uproot hundreds of trees as settlers attack Palestinians across the occupied West Bank: Nablus: Israeli settlers a Palestinian school in Jalud, forcing the evacuation of students, and attacked nearby olive harvesters on Monday, WAFA reported. In Qaryut, Israeli soldiers shot a Palestinian in the shoulder following a settler attack. Hebron: Israeli forces agricultural structures, uprooted more than 300 trees, and bulldozed over 2.5 acres of farmland north of Hebron. Forces also detained a Palestinian and two foreign activists documenting a settler attack in Masafer Yatta. Soldiers detained teachers heading to a school in Susiya, arresting one and confiscating their vehicle. Ramallah: Settlers and attempted to burn two homes in Turmus Ayya, beating and injuring a Palestinian-American man. Another Palestinian was injured in a settler assault in Deir Abu Mashal. Jenin: Israeli forces more than 20 demolition notices targeting agricultural and commercial structures, while settlers expelled farmers from their land in Al-Arqa. Israeli settlers attack European diplomats observing olive harvest in West Bank: Masked Israeli settlers on all-terrain vehicles European diplomats and Palestinian farmers during the olive harvest near Taybeh, a Palestinian Christian village northeast of Ramallah, on Saturday. Diplomats from France, including the French consul in Jerusalem, Belgium, and Poland were present. The settlers surrounded a diplomatic vehicle and demanded ID, then pelted it with stones and smashed a window of a Belgian consulate car, according to the Israeli Army Radio. Footage shows men carrying clubs approaching the diplomats and one diplomat lying on the ground. The attack came a day after settlers beat and shot Palestinians and brutally assaulted Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine also during the harvest. Reporter Jasper Nathaniel wrote an account of that assault . In the wake of international criticism following the two attacks, Israeli security forces said they arrested 10 suspects in connection with the violence. Israeli settlers are rarely arrested or prosecuted for attacks on Palestinians. Iran Russian Foreign Minister visits Iran: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov is Tehran on Monday for talks on bilateral relations and regional and international developments, Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said. Lavrov will outline Moscow's efforts to "de-escalate regional tensions created by the United States and Israel," according to the Russian state news agency. The visit follows consultations between Moscow and Washington and Lavrov's participation in a ministerial meeting with Gulf Cooperation Council countries. In an October 9 call between Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump, Putin conveyed Iran's position on possible ways to resolve the conflict, according to the Kremlin. Oil tanker hits naval mine near Hormuz, catches fire, IRGC says: An oil tanker a naval mine south of the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, causing an explosion and fire in its engine room, according to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy. The IRGC claimed the vessel had switched off its navigation and positioning systems and was attempting to exit the strait through an unauthorized southern route. Pakistan suspends trade with Iran at two major border crossings: Pakistan trade with Iran through the Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan border crossings, leaving hundreds of trucks carrying liquefied petroleum gas, rice, fruit and other commodities stranded on both sides of the border. Pakistani officials cited security concerns, smuggling prevention and administrative improvements, while Iran's Foreign Ministry attributed the disruption to "technical issues." Both countries said consultations were underway to restore normal operations. Following the start of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, Islamabad and Tehran introduced measures to expand cross-border commerce, including streamlined customs procedures and new transit routes. In August, both governments agreed to work toward keeping border crossings open around the clock. Lebanon Israeli airstrikes, artillery, and machine-gun fire target southern Lebanon despite ceasefire: Israeli warplanes Kfar Tebnit in Nabatieh district overnight, while Israeli forces a large demolition operation in Beit Yahoun and shelled the outskirts of Braashit, both in Bint Jbeil district. Israeli artillery also targeted Mansouri in Tyre (Sour) district, while troops opened machine-gun fire toward Beit al-Siyad and Mansouri, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. On Monday morning, Israeli troops opened machine-gun fire toward Wadi Beit Lif and Srebbine in Bint Jbeil district. U.S. News Trump endorses Netanyahu days before Israel 's Oct. 27 election: President Donald Trump Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday, calling him "a Great Warrior Prime Minister, and an even greater Partner for Peace in combating the Islamic Republic of Iran." Trump had held back on an endorsement for months, telling a Time interviewer as recently as this month that he's "not involved in politics anymore." In the same post, Trump again threatened to "soon finish the job" against Iran "unless they change their ways, rapidly," but said that if Israel has "anyone other than Bibi," then "America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so." Trump puts newly signed Russia sanctions on hold, citing national interest : Trump an executive order Friday pausing a sweeping Russia sanctions package, telling Congress the delay was in the national interest. He signed the legislation last month, and the pause comes two days before the deadline for implementation. Named for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham , who died unexpectedly in July after returning from Ukraine, the bill was drafted with Sen. Richard Blumenthal(D-Conn.) and passed with bipartisan majorities. The package targeted Russian officials, banks, and the "shadow fleet" of tankers moving Russian energy. It also imposed tariffs of up to 100% on the top five importers of Russian oil or gas, with an exception for countries that import less than 15% of their natural gas from Russia and are significantly cutting those imports. FAA bars unauthorized drones along U.S.-Mexico border: The FAA is a temporary flight restriction that bars unauthorized drone activity up to 400 feet above ground level, extending one nautical mile north of the U.S.-Mexico border. In April, the FAA and Pentagon signed an agreement allowing the government to use a high-energy laser counter-drone system along the southern border. The Pentagon claimed more than 1,000 drone incursions along the border each month, and U.S. security officials have grown alarmed about cartels using drones to drop drugs or surveil trafficking routes. In February, the FAA briefly halted El Paso's airport because Customs and Border Protection used the laser without a safety review. Days later, the military shot down a CBP drone with the laser, and the FAA expanded its restricted area around Fort Hancock, Texas. Mexican man found dead at Laredo ICE facility, seventh ICE detainee death in Texas this year : Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias , 56, was unresponsive in his cell at the Rio Grande Processing Center around 10 a.m. on Saturday, his daughter and Rep. Henry Cuellar (D-Texas) told the Texas Tribune. He is the seventh person to die in ICE detention in Texas this year. The Rio Grande Processing Center is managed by GEO Group, which declined to comment on the story. The family learned of his death through the Webb County Medical Examiner and was not contacted by federal agencies. Andrade-Covarrubias had a heart condition, diabetes, and high blood pressure, but, his daughter alleged, staff wouldn't administer his medication. Obama condemns Trump administration 's investigation of Rep. Ilhan Omar: Former President Barack Obama the investigation of Rep. Ilhan Omar(D-Minn.) in a statement on X on Sunday. He said, "the fact that any president, or any administration, is willing to engage in such transparent efforts to intimidate someone should outrage all Americans, regardless of how they feel about Congresswoman Omar's political views." He warned that "if this becomes the new normal, there's no reason to believe it will stop with her -- or that future presidents, in either party, won't do the same." Federal agents raided Omar's Washington home last week and seized her phone as part of an investigation into whether she or her late father gave false information on immigration paperwork 26 years ago. The administration intends to build a case to strip her citizenship and ultimately deport her, the Wall Street Journal reported. The first Trump administration reviewed similar allegations in 2019 and found insufficient evidence for a full investigation, the Washington Post reported. Trump says California officials "will all go to jail" if state counts ballots of supposed noncitizens: Trump on Truth Social Friday that California officials "will all go to jail for a long period of time!!!" if they include in their midterm count the mail-in ballots of people the federal government claims are noncitizens. On Thursday, the Justice Department announced that it was pursuing legal action against California, after DOJ gave officials 48 hours to review the citizenship status of about 20,000 voters. Texas reportedly weighed selling Boca Chica State Park to SpaceX: The Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission selling a 1,300-acre state park, the beachfront Boca Chica State Park in Cameron County, to SpaceX, Texas Monthly reported. According to a draft agenda, the commission planned to take up the sale in closed-door executive session on November 5, two days after the midterm election. After Texas Monthly inquired about the sale, a spokesperson for the commission said it "is not considering the sale of the Boca Chica property at its November meeting." She did not answer follow-up questions about the talks, Elon Musk 's involvement, why the agenda changed, or whether the issue is shelved. Sources said the nine commissioners, all appointed by Gov. Greg Abbott , could take it up later. Lawmakers gave SpaceX partial control of Boca Chica's beaches last year, and in 2024 the state agreed to a 43-acre swap that SpaceX later abandoned. This summer the US Fish and Wildlife Service approved giving SpaceX 715 acres of the Lower Rio Grande Valley National Wildlife Refuge for 683 acres elsewhere. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Ukraine launches 1,000+ drones at Russia; Russian strikes on Ukraine kill two: Russia's Defense Ministry it "neutralized" 1,015 Ukrainian drones overnight. St. Petersburg Gov. Alexander Beglov said a "massive" strike killed at least one person and injured five. Some of the Ukrainian strikes appeared to target energy and tech infrastructure. Several residential buildings and two houses were struck. About 20,000 people lost power in the Leningrad Oblast, the region's governor said. In Kyiv, Russian strikes overnight killed a woman, hit a subway station, and damaged a residential building, injuring three people. Russian attacks on Zaporizhzhia killed a woman and wounded at least two people, including a six-year-old girl. 2,400+ arrested in French protests: Protests against education policies and the rising cost of living in France over the weekend with some of the largest turnouts since the demonstrations began last month, with hundreds of thousands taking to the streets in some 140 cities and towns. Police have arrested at least 2,400 protesters since Saturday. French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said he has asked regional authorities to impose partial curfews in some cities. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez offered his resignation on Sunday but President Emmanuel Macron asked him to stay in his position to respond to the situation. Macron blamed much of Saturday's violence on "insurrectionist elements from radical far-left groups, joined by numerous criminals," he said in a televised address on Sunday. "Those who looted will have to pay for the damage, and those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable," he added. RSF attack kills at least 11 displaced people: A Rapid Support Forces attack near the Chad border at least 11 internally displaced people and wounded dozens more on Saturday, the Sudan Tribune reported. Most of the casualties were women and children, according to the Darfur Regional Government. Albanian police attack protesters, arrest 1,000+: Police in Tirana what appeared to be rubber bullets at protesters Saturday outside the education ministry. The protests are focused on perceived government corruption, lack of jobs, and poor education standards. Rounds hit several demonstrators and two Reuters journalists. The chief of police did not deny using rubber bullets, saying "all means that were used were employed in a limited manner." He said that authorities have arrested 1,067 people and prosecuted 388. 19 dead, 25 injured in stampede during Hindu religious festival in Kolkata: At least 19 people were killed and 25 were injured in a stampede at a Hindu religious festival in Kolkata, India, on Saturday. Police said a crowd outside a pavilion took cover from rain, and that some worshippers fell in the rush and were trampled. Victims were taken to Kolkata Medical College, according to Suvendu Adhikari, the head of West Bengal province. A seven-year-old girl was among the dead. Sisi says his term ends in 2030, proposes military academy program to train future leaders: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi pledged on Saturday at an Egyptian Military Academy graduation that he would leave office after his term ends in 2030, calling it "a matter that has been completely settled and will not be discussed," and reiterated that the constitution will not be amended again. Sisi, 71, was reelected in December 2023 to a six-year term, after amending the constitution in 2019 to extend presidential terms from four to six years and permitted him to run for a third term. In the past two elections, several opposition candidates have been jailed or barred from running. A former army general, Sisi became president in 2014, a year after toppling elected president Mohamed Morsi. Sisi also announced a plan for his succession, saying that only candidates aged 40 to 50 with a doctorate should apply and would be required to spend 30 months at a military academy training program. Lula and Bolsonaro face off in debate: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro their first face-to-face debate Sunday, a week before the October 25 runoff election. Bolsonaro finished nearly two points ahead of Lula in the first round of voting. According to a new , Bolsonaro only leads Lula 46.5% to 45.9%--well within the poll's margin of error. Mexico arrests former Chihuahua official, charges treason: Mexican authorities Cesar Jauregui, Chihuahua's former attorney general, on suspicion of treason, Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said Saturday. Prosecutors say that earlier this year, he allowed U.S. agents to take part in an "irregular" raid on a suspected drug laboratory in the border state without the required legal authorization. In April, the U.S. said that two embassy employees in Mexico City had died. Reuters reported that they were CIA officers. Anti-corruption lawyer shot dead in Guatemala City: Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa, an anti-corruption lawyer and former prosecutor, was shot and at a sports center in Guatemala City on Saturday, Reuters reported. Police said that they detained two men and seized a carbine-style firearm and a motorcycle in connection with the case. Solorzano Foppa led criminal investigations in the Public Prosecutor's Office, and later led the federal tax authority, prosecuting dozens of powerful business figures and recovering unpaid taxes. In 2025, he alleged links between the Barrio 18 gang and the right-wing political party National Unity of Hope. He also reported connections between criminal gangs and the judicial system. Venezuelan opposition reaffirms support for exiled political figure Machado: The Venezuelan opposition coalition known as the Unitary Democratic Platform to "recognize and support the leadership of Maria Corina Machado" and renewed their demand for "free elections" in the country on Sunday. Machado has lived in exile since December, and her party says Venezuelan authorities have blocked her repeated attempts to come back. Machado told the Financial Times she wants elections to be held by July next year. Kenya reports eighth Ebola case: A middle-aged man tested positive for Ebola, Kenya's Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth Sunday, bringing the tally of infections to eight. Amoth added that the man was likely exposed to Ebola by Kenya's patient zero, who had arrived from Democratic Republic of Congo earlier this month. Congo reports over 9,400 Ebola cases and over 4,500 deaths. Fire at Canadian military base kills four, hospitalizes dozens: A fast-moving grass fire four service members at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta, Canada, on Saturday. subject: I’m humbly asking you

body:
All I need is a minute to explain.
#

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q42026.PjNIJI&refcode=em261019-1-b&t=1&akid=11948%2E3935704%2Eim4RPA)
---
Hello,
I am humbly asking you to pitch in your first donation of $15 to GIFFORDS PAC before midnight. It’s been 15 years since I was shot in Tucson, Arizona. Today also marks exactly 15 days from the November election, and I am hoping to get the largest number of individual donations we can in our fight against gun violence.
If that is all you need to hear — and you are fired up like I am — you can use this link to donate:
**[https://go.giffords.org/go/Stand-With-Gabby](https://go.giffords.org/go/64441?c0=giff-em-q42026.BxBX_u&refcode=em261019-1-b&t=2&akid=11948%2E3935704%2Eim4RPA)**
While you probably didn’t wake up this morning thinking you would chip in to help end gun violence, that is the ask I have of you today. Let me explain.
Poll after poll shows that an overwhelming majority of voters support commonsense gun safety legislation. Our politicians must find the courage to act and protect our communities.
If they fail to do so, then we must vote them out in 15 days and elect leaders who will. That’s why I am asking:
$15 to help mobilize and reach persuadable voters — online and at their doorstep.
$15 to fight back against overreach from the Trump administration and Republicans, including efforts to pass a nationwide concealed carry mandate.
$15 to help us elect a gun safety majority.
Our gun lobby adversaries are spending whatever it takes to drown out our movement. The only way we can overcome their attacks is with your support.
**So I am asking you directly:** [**Will you contribute $15 (or more, if you can afford it) to GIFFORDS PAC today?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/64441?c0=giff-em-q42026.BxBX_u&refcode=em261019-1-b&t=3&akid=11948%2E3935704%2Eim4RPA)

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

# “I trust Reed—and you should too.”
_-Rita Albrecht_
---
| | **I stand beside Reed.** He stands up for us, our community, and looks out for our neighbors.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Reed has shown us that improving people’s lives is one of his strongest values. He’s a trusted leader who sees a problem and rallies the resources and people needed to address it and solve it.
* When he learned that renters were being taken advantage of, he worked alongside others to organize a tenants’ group.
* In response to too many tragic deaths of our unhoused community members, Reed worked to organize the grassroots effort to create an emergency shelter more than a decade ago.
* Then when it became clear that community needs were greater than what the shelter could provide, Reed and his board renovated a former clinic building to open the Day Center.

**Reed is a valued community leader.** People know and trust Reed because he has been helping people in our community for more than 20 years. And he is a trusted resource for people across the region and state who reach out to Reed for his advice and counsel about how to better serve the homeless populations in their communities.**People are excited – let’s keep that momentum going.** While knocking on doors together Sunday, we heard clearly that Reed’s campaign is resonating with people! Area residents are ready to elect a representative who they can trust and will truly work for them. And the opposition knows it.That’s why, as we get close to the election, attacks against Reed are getting ugly. The closer we get to the election, the uglier they are. They are not a reflection of who he is.I’ve been knocking doors with Reed all summer and met many people who are excited to vote for Reed. This weekend, we found that has not changed.As we head full speed into the last days of the campaign, I’ll continue to stand beside Reed because I trust Reed – and you should too.I stand beside Reed because he has proven himself to be a selfless community leader and that’s exactly the kind of representative I want working for me in St. Paul._Rita Albrecht_

#### **[Jackson Defends Telling Collins to'Shut Up' During Cringeworthy CNN Interview](https://substack.com/redirect/a0fa9cb7-a2f2-400f-8922-995af61e85fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Troy Jackson went on CNN's "State of the Union" Sunday and told Dana Bash he doesn't regret telling Susan Collins to shut up. That wasn't even the worst part of his performance. Jackson sat on his stool like a high school bully in the principal's office, writhing in discomfort with no control over his body language or facial expressions. According to Jackson, Collins had it coming because she was getting a little uppity with her backtalk on the stage. His explanation: Collins suggested the debate heckler was one of his supporters, and he isn't going to be "talked down to by Senator Collins." Bash asked one more time whether he was leaving it there, with no apology. Jackson: "Yes." The man knows his brand. In Collins' defense, anyone who speaks in complete sentences will appear to be talking down to Action Jackson...

#### **[Maine Sends $300 Affordability Checks to Foreign Seasonal Workers Who Left U.S.](https://substack.com/redirect/57918358-08ea-4b83-9922-9b341d18ecbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
An Old Orchard Beach employer handed Jon Fetherston photos of eight $300 state affordability checks, dated Aug. 7 through Aug. 20. He says they were mailed to J-1 visa workers who spent the summer here and then went home, and that the checks are still sitting uncashed at his business. The law behind the payments, LD 2212, says you qualify only if you filed a 2025 Maine return as a full-year resident by Oct. 15, 2026. Exactly as I predicted when Maine Democrats first proposed the $1.2 billion omnibus package earlier this year, Maine tax dollars are going to non-citizens. Based on the number of non-citizens present in Maine, this could amount to $5 million in taxpayer "stimmies" -- even more depending on how many illegal aliens are getting the checks. Keep working, sucker!

#### **[Home Sweet Home Care: Another Somali-Run Homecare Business Co-Located with a Medical Transport Company](https://substack.com/redirect/6c667fb1-86d2-4dd9-96e9-9332c44a0a08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Qamar Ahmed of South Portland runs two home care companies out of Suite 2 at 1717 Congress Street in Portland. One of them, Home Sweet Home Care, has billed MaineCare $2,692,922 since 2020, including $772,863 last year, and has been operating since March on a pending license renewal the state hasn't ruled on. The other, Platinum Home Health Care, has no state license, though its website calls it "Medicare-certified" and "state-licensed" and posts glowing patient testimonials. Asked about those reviews, Ahmed first told us "those were me," then said they were from patients who knew her work elsewhere, then hung up when we read her one that named Platinum. She had also agreed to meet us at her office on Oct. 8; the door was locked. A medical courier tied to the business, Medwave Express, is registered at her home and was administratively dissolved in August. Maine Wire reporter Seamus Othot has the latest details.
#### **[Sen. Elizabeth Warren Joins Troy Jackson at Portland Rally as Maine Sees Another Round of'No Kings' Demonstrations](https://substack.com/redirect/a4602a2b-c4dd-4977-b8fb-61d4933e0b81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Right after Collins landed an endorsement from the Passamaquoddy tribe, Jackson stumped with Liz Warren, aka Pocahontas -- real Indians versus the fake Indian! Jackson's campaign called its event a "Defeat Collins Rally," and Greater Freeport Indivisible said that partisan billing is exactly why it wasn't an official No Kings event. Warren, who originally called Graham Platner "my kind of man," came up from Massachusetts to tell the crowd it could have "a rubber stamp for a wannabe king" or "a fighter for the people." Leftists held about 30 events around the state, including roughly 400 people in Bath with Angus King. Freeport drew about 75, down from the roughly 3,000 a local organizer reported at earlier rallies. Nationally, the "No Kings" rally day was a bit of a fizzle, according to Bluesky users.

#### **[Northern Maine to Receive $37M in Federal Funding for Freight Rail Upgrades](https://substack.com/redirect/89fd233c-ce06-4501-82fc-e123edcd31b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
MaineDOT is getting more than $37 million from the Federal Railroad Administration to rebuild about 90 miles of track around Fort Kent, Madawaska and Van Buren, on the Maine Northern and Eastern Maine railways. That means new rail, ties and ballast, plus work on a key railroad bridge. Collins and King sent the FRA a letter backing the application.
#### **[OCP Warns Medical Cannabis Users of Unsafe Levels of Mold, Bacteria and Yeast in Company's Product](https://substack.com/redirect/f8ea63a3-fb8d-4dae-9f4f-a3453dc7a3fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
After a complaint, the Office of Cannabis Policy tested flower and pre-rolls from The B Maine, a Lebanon dispensary formerly known as Dr. Melo's, and found unsafe levels of mold, yeast and bacteria in six strains. In one "Cherry AK" pre-roll, the yeast and mold were "too numerous to be counted." OCP can't order recalls in the medical program, so it put out a patient advisory instead. The dispensary is cooperating and gave up the bad product to be destroyed. If you bought "Florida Oranges" or "Skunk Hero" there lately, read the advisory.
#### **[El Presidente Torches El-Sayed](https://substack.com/redirect/d3b9e9dc-5400-4dad-92fd-95f577191b96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Dave Portnoy went on Fox News' "The Sunday Briefing" and unloaded on Abdul El-Sayed, the Democrats' Senate nominee in Michigan: "This guy makes me puke. Everything about him makes me puke." Portnoy, a Michigan alum, says he wouldn't send his niece and nephew there if El-Sayed wins, because he doesn't want them "worried about getting harassed for being Jewish." Maine has been on the business end of El Presidente before. In May, Graham Platner's campaign asked him to help push a Red Sox-themed ad, and his reply brought up the tattoo Platner later covered. Portnoy, who has traditionally eschewed politics, has become increasingly acid-tongued toward Democratic politicians as the party has embraced antisemitism.
#### **[Vassalboro Man Critically Injured in Three-Vehicle Crash on Maine Turnpike](https://substack.com/redirect/d789e027-f412-4e5d-8284-ce8755dd3190?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Just before midnight Saturday, Devon Thomas, 24, of Vassalboro lost control of his Hyundai Elantra heading south on the Turnpike in Falmouth, hit several guardrails and stopped in the middle of the highway, State Police say. A Ford Explorer driven by a 36-year-old from Portland and a Ford Fusion driven by a 22-year-old from Lewiston both struck his car. Thomas was critically injured, and the injured drivers were taken to Maine Medical Center. Troopers are still investigating.

Top news and headlines from around the state, brought to you by The Robinson Report. Oct 19 | | | | | | | | | | | Troy Jackson went on CNN's "State of the Union" Sunday and told Dana Bash he doesn't regret telling Susan Collins to shut up. That wasn't even the worst part of his performance. Jackson sat on his stool like a high school bully in the principal's office, writhing in discomfort with no control over his body language or facial expressions. According to Jackson, Collins had it coming because she was getting a little uppity with her backtalk on the stage. His explanation: Collins suggested the debate heckler was one of his supporters, and he isn't going to be "talked down to by Senator Collins." Bash asked one more time whether he was leaving it there, with no apology. Jackson: "Yes." The man knows his brand. In Collins' defense, anyone who speaks in complete sentences will appear to be talking down to Action Jackson... An Old Orchard Beach employer handed Jon Fetherston photos of eight $300 state affordability checks, dated Aug. 7 through Aug. 20. He says they were mailed to J-1 visa workers who spent the summer here and then went home, and that the checks are still sitting uncashed at his business. The law behind the payments, LD 2212, says you qualify only if you filed a 2025 Maine return as a full-year resident by Oct. 15, 2026. Exactly as I predicted when Maine Democrats first proposed the $1.2 billion omnibus package earlier this year, Maine tax dollars are going to non-citizens. Based on the number of non-citizens present in Maine, this could amount to $5 million in taxpayer "stimmies" -- even more depending on how many illegal aliens are getting the checks. Keep working, sucker! Like this kind of reporting? Subscribe to The Robinson Report for the latest news moving Maine politics. Qamar Ahmed of South Portland runs two home care companies out of Suite 2 at 1717 Congress Street in Portland. One of them, Home Sweet Home Care, has billed MaineCare $2,692,922 since 2020, including $772,863 last year, and has been operating since March on a pending license renewal the state hasn't ruled on. The other, Platinum Home Health Care, has no state license, though its website calls it "Medicare-certified" and "state-licensed" and posts glowing patient testimonials. Asked about those reviews, Ahmed first told us "those were me," then said they were from patients who knew her work elsewhere, then hung up when we read her one that named Platinum. She had also agreed to meet us at her office on Oct. 8; the door was locked. A medical courier tied to the business, Medwave Express, is registered at her home and was administratively dissolved in August. Maine Wire reporter Seamus Othot has the latest details. Right after Collins landed an endorsement from the Passamaquoddy tribe, Jackson stumped with Liz Warren, aka Pocahontas -- real Indians versus the fake Indian! Jackson's campaign called its event a "Defeat Collins Rally," and Greater Freeport Indivisible said that partisan billing is exactly why it wasn't an official No Kings event. Warren, who originally called Graham Platner "my kind of man," came up from Massachusetts to tell the crowd it could have "a rubber stamp for a wannabe king" or "a fighter for the people." Leftists held about 30 events around the state, including roughly 400 people in Bath with Angus King. Freeport drew about 75, down from the roughly 3,000 a local organizer reported at earlier rallies. Nationally, the "No Kings" rally day was a bit of a fizzle, according to Bluesky users. MaineDOT is getting more than $37 million from the Federal Railroad Administration to rebuild about 90 miles of track around Fort Kent, Madawaska and Van Buren, on the Maine Northern and Eastern Maine railways. That means new rail, ties and ballast, plus work on a key railroad bridge. Collins and King sent the FRA a letter backing the application. After a complaint, the Office of Cannabis Policy tested flower and pre-rolls from The B Maine, a Lebanon dispensary formerly known as Dr. Melo's, and found unsafe levels of mold, yeast and bacteria in six strains. In one "Cherry AK" pre-roll, the yeast and mold were "too numerous to be counted." OCP can't order recalls in the medical program, so it put out a patient advisory instead. The dispensary is cooperating and gave up the bad product to be destroyed. If you bought "Florida Oranges" or "Skunk Hero" there lately, read the advisory. Dave Portnoy went on Fox News' "The Sunday Briefing" and unloaded on Abdul El-Sayed, the Democrats' Senate nominee in Michigan: "This guy makes me puke. Everything about him makes me puke." Portnoy, a Michigan alum, says he wouldn't send his niece and nephew there if El-Sayed wins, because he doesn't want them "worried about getting harassed for being Jewish." Maine has been on the business end of El Presidente before. In May, Graham Platner's campaign asked him to help push a Red Sox-themed ad, and his reply brought up the tattoo Platner later covered. Portnoy, who has traditionally eschewed politics, has become increasingly acid-tongued toward Democratic politicians as the party has embraced antisemitism. Just before midnight Saturday, Devon Thomas, 24, of Vassalboro lost control of his Hyundai Elantra heading south on the Turnpike in Falmouth, hit several guardrails and stopped in the middle of the highway, State Police say. A Ford Explorer driven by a 36-year-old from Portland and a Ford Fusion driven by a 22-year-old from Lewiston both struck his car. Thomas was critically injured, and the injured drivers were taken to Maine Medical Center. Troopers are still investigating. Videos from @TheMaineWire on X : Twenty-eight seconds of CNN's "State of the Union." Bash asks if he regrets it, and Jackson says no: Collins accused him of setting the heckler up, and he "had no idea who it was." Our most-watched upload on Sunday. : Our caption, quoting RNC Research's clip from the same interview: "I'm going to take away your health plan is indeed a bold election strategy." In the clip, Jackson says private plans could stick around for "elective surgeries and things like that," but basic care goes under Medicare for All, and "everyone has to get into the plan." Our most-liked post on Sunday. Maine Wire TV If you 're reading this, you probably get Maine Wire TV delivered via Substack. But you can also watch us on Facebook, X, and . You can subscribe on Apple or Spotify, too! Here's Friday's episode. : Friday's full episode, all 68 minutes of it. The Maine Wire on WVOM (Monday, about 12 minutes) I joined Ric Tyler this morning to talk about the $300 checks. My read is that the Mills administration mailed them off Maine Revenue Services' list of 2025 tax filers, and in my words, "They didn't filter out non-citizens. They didn't even filter out dead people." A host said, "Now, granted, eight snapshots of checks is a pretty small sample, but it doesn't dismiss the idea that this could be as big as you suggest it is." The segment closes on a drawing for a Maine Wire fleece in this week's College of Political Knowledge. Today's Political Events 1. Eastport data center deadline, today : Comments and motions to intervene are due to FERC by 5 p.m. today, Mon., Oct. 19 , on DeepGreen's preliminary permit for a subsea AI data center in Eastport's coastal waters. The city of Eastport, the National Marine Fisheries Service and Save Passamaquoddy Bay are among those that have moved to intervene. 2. AOC comes to Portland : Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Troy Jackson hold a "Students vs. Billionaires Town Hall" at the State Theatre, Thu., Oct. 22, 2 p.m. 5. Voting : No-excuse absentee and early in-person voting run through Thu., Oct. 29 , the same day as the Pingree-Russell CD1 debate. clean_body: Another unprecedented step to harm our right to vote| | | | | | Team, opponents of voting rights are getting desperate. They are so worried about catastrophic losses in the midterms that they keep threatening to deploy ICE agents to polling locations across the country, the same way we've had to watch them invade cities like Minneapolis, Chicago, and Los Angeles. This is a fact: It is illegal for federal officers to be posted to polling places, especially if they're ordered there to intimidate voters or interfere with ongoing elections. We know how little respect the vote suppressors have for the law, so we're doing all we can to ensure free and fair elections nationwide and to make every vote count. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | | = | | = | | = | | | Former Trump advisor Steve Bannon threatened to have ICE at the polls months ago. Former U.S. Senator and current DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin keeps talking about it. Opponents of voting rights in various states are considering making requests or sending state officials. We even saw in recent elections where local vigilantes in states like Arizona stood armed outside polling places , questioning anyone they saw that they didn't think should vote. Or similar groups that stood watch over ballot drop boxes to intimidate eligible voters returning their ballots. We even saw cases where ballot drop boxes were set on fire. We're committed to protecting our fundamental right to vote however we can. We want to increase participation in our elections through information and voter registration, not turn people away. We have to step up and fight inequities in voting wherever we can. = | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country. Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities. = = Contributions or gifts to Integrity First Voter Action Project are not tax deductible as charitable contributions or as business expenses under IRC Section 162(3). Today is a special day for the Goldstein family.
Thanks for reading The Goldstein Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..AvrCu1--HUcs99LR903W7LV4PQTd1waq94mpyXMw5E8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=221160565)
For the first time, my father, Dr. Michael Goldstein, and I are on the general election ballot together.
My father is running for Congress. I'm running for State Representative in Greenwich.
But this campaign has become about something much bigger than politics.
It's about family.
Over the past several months, we've knocked on doors, attended community events, met neighbors, exchanged ideas, and spent more time together than we probably have in years.
And I have to say -- it's been a blast.
There is something truly special about a father and son sharing an experience like this. We don't agree on everything. We have different perspectives, different experiences, and occasionally different ways of doing things. But we share the same values and a belief that public service should be about something greater than ourselves.
My father has spent more than four decades caring for people as a physician. I've spent my career working in law, business, and construction. We took different professional paths, but we both believe in giving back to the communities that helped shape us.
And now, we're sharing a campaign trail.
What This Is Really About
As I've walked through Greenwich, I've thought a great deal about what we're trying to preserve for the next generation.
The opportunity to grow up in a community you love.
The ability to afford a home, raise a family, and build a career.
The freedom to pursue your ambitions without feeling that you have to leave Connecticut to find opportunity.
And the simple privilege of spending time with the people who matter most.
That's what this campaign means to me. Preserving family, protecting our communities, and creating opportunity for the next generation.
My father and I may be running for two different offices, but these are the values that brought us both into public service.
The Best Part of This Campaign
Years from now, I don't know whether I'll remember every speech, debate, or campaign event.
But I know I'll remember the time spent with my father.
The conversations between stops. The laughter. The long days knocking on doors. The people we've met. And the opportunity to experience all of it together.
Not everyone gets to share something like this with a parent, and I don't take a moment of it for granted.
Whatever happens on November 3, those memories will last a lifetime.
Today, We Begin Voting
Early voting begins today, October 19, and continues through November 1. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3.
The father-son Goldstein ticket is on the ballot:
Dr. Michael Goldstein -- U.S. Congress, Connecticut's 4th District
Jonathan Goldstein -- State Representative, Connecticut's 150th District
Two generations. Two different offices. One family with a shared commitment to public service.
To everyone who has opened a door, shared a concern, offered encouragement, or simply taken the time to speak with us -- thank you.
And to my father, thank you for the years of lessons, the example you've set, and the opportunity to share this extraordinary experience.
At the end of the day, elections come and go. Family is what lasts.
And that is what makes this journey so special.
Jonathan Goldstein

Thanks for reading The Goldstein Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. For the first time, my father, Dr. Michael Goldstein, and I are on the general election ballot together. My father is running for Congress. I'm running for State Representative in Greenwich. But this campaign has become about something much bigger than politics. It's about family. Over the past several months, we've knocked on doors, attended community events, met neighbors, exchanged ideas, and spent more time together than we probably have in years. And I have to say -- it's been a blast. There is something truly special about a father and son sharing an experience like this. We don't agree on everything. We have different perspectives, different experiences, and occasionally different ways of doing things. But we share the same values and a belief that public service should be about something greater than ourselves. My father has spent more than four decades caring for people as a physician. I've spent my career working in law, business, and construction. We took different professional paths, but we both believe in giving back to the communities that helped shape us. And now, we're sharing a campaign trail. What This Is Really About As I've walked through Greenwich, I've thought a great deal about what we're trying to preserve for the next generation. The opportunity to grow up in a community you love. The ability to afford a home, raise a family, and build a career. The freedom to pursue your ambitions without feeling that you have to leave Connecticut to find opportunity. And the simple privilege of spending time with the people who matter most. That's what this campaign means to me. Preserving family, protecting our communities, and creating opportunity for the next generation. My father and I may be running for two different offices, but these are the values that brought us both into public service. The Best Part of This Campaign Years from now, I don't know whether I'll remember every speech, debate, or campaign event. But I know I'll remember the time spent with my father. The conversations between stops. The laughter. The long days knocking on doors. The people we've met. And the opportunity to experience all of it together. Not everyone gets to share something like this with a parent, and I don't take a moment of it for granted. Whatever happens on November 3, those memories will last a lifetime. Family is what lasts. And that is what makes this journey so special. body:
We turned a long shot into a dead heat. Now we need to finish it.
Peter,
**A new poll just came out showing me ahead of Greg Abbott, 47% to 45%.**
That’s the fifth poll in the last month to show us leading this race. Not tied. Ahead.
If you’d told me a year ago, when we launched this campaign, that we’d be here, I’m not sure I would have believed you. But here we are, and it’s because of people like you.
**[So I’m asking: will you split $5 between Small Town PAC and my campaign today to keep this momentum going?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_small_town_pac.utc88R&amount=5&refcode=em20261019-1227&t=1&akid=1227%2E34582%2EYrZZTa)**
Here’s what the numbers tell me:
Texans know Greg Abbott, and they’re tired of him. 52% of likely voters view him unfavorably, and only 44% favorably. **After more than a decade of corruption that’s left Texas families to fend for themselves, voters across the political spectrum are ready for change.**
And the more Texans get to know me, the more they like what they see. My name ID has jumped to 79% in just the last few weeks, and I’m still viewed favorably by a 12-point margin (45% to 33%), even after Abbott has spent millions attacking me.
Grassroots donations from supporters like you made that possible. **[Will you make a donation split between Small Town PAC and my campaign so we can reach the voters who still don’t know me?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_small_town_pac.utc88R&amount=5&refcode=em20261019-1227&t=2&akid=1227%2E34582%2EYrZZTa)**
Together, we’ve turned this race from a long shot into a dead heat. A few months ago, people said we’d never get this close to taking Texas back. Now we’re on the edge of making history.
But Abbott knows it too. He’s raised more than $141 million in this campaign and already spent over $120 million of it trying to stop us. He still has $17 million left to spend on false attack ads right as voting begins. **The undecided voters who will decide this race are about to be buried in them, and we need to make sure they hear from us too.**
Now is the time for your donation to have the largest impact. **[Can you make a donation split between Small Town PAC and my campaign so we can stay on the air in the final weeks?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=partner_ms_gh_em_small_town_pac.utc88R&amount=5&refcode=em20261019-1227&t=3&akid=1227%2E34582%2EYrZZTa)**

Thank you,
Gina

On her first birthday, my granddaughter received the _maqel_ , not as a toy but as the staff of life. She crawls toward it now and again, a boisterous babble beginning a conversation that will span decades.
As she grows, she will inherit the names of those who came before, learning the weight of the lives that carved the path she walks. By her thirteenth year, she will realize that while her ancestors provided the map, she must hold the compass--and only then, will she write her own name.
Heritage provides the roots, but it does not dictate the direction. To hold the _maqel_ is to accept the burden of self-governance, the necessity of choosing good over evil. The names of the past cannot walk the path for her.
We are defined by what Steinbeck called "the great choice." We are directed by the command to "Choose life."
Every kitchen table holds a story. The choices we make write it.
**Pause. Breathe. Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

| **Know Before You Vote, Vol. 4**
**_Does Tourism help or hurt Vermont?_**
How candidates view tourism – and how we view the small businesses and workers in this sector – is another important indication of our core economic philosophy and vision for the future.

**I believe we need a Vermont where more young people, working families, and small family-owned businesses can thrive. **
** **__Help us get the Governor over the finish line on November 3rd with a donation today by clicking the link below. __****
To do that we must support the farms, restaurants, inns, cafes, breweries, ski areas, and recreation trails that attract visitors from across the country and around the world.

Together, they provide jobs and tax revenue and create enormous economic benefits for our State. In fact, it is one of our most stable economic sectors.

**I saw my opponent described tourism as "extractive,” at the World’s Fair in Tunbridge... which itself creates great economic activity from out of state visitors for the region every year. ****

Like me, you might wonder what “extractive” means? It’s a term some people use to describe when resources are taken from a community, without economic value being returned.

**Now, I see it differently, because tourism in Vermont supports hundreds of small businesses, employs tens of thousands of Vermonters, and helps rural communities across our state. **

**In 2024, for example, visitors:**
* Spent **$4.2 BILLION** at Vermont businesses;
* Supported nearly **32,000** **JOBS** ; and
* Generated an estimated **$293.5 MILLION** in state and local taxes.

I’ve spent decades listening to Vermont’s employers, supporting our hospitality and recreation sectors, and working to make Vermont a place where more people can afford to live, work, raise a family, and retire.

**Vermont’s future depends on GROWING our economy, not dismissing entire sectors that help make economic growth possible in every part of Vermont. **

And in the campaign for governor the choice could not be clearer.

**That’s something to know before you vote.**

**Oh, and one more thing... if not for tourism, and Tom Watson’s love for our ski mountains, IBM would not have been built in Vermont... think about that.

Thanks -

Gov. Phil Scott**
**__Help us get the Governor over the finish line on November 3rd with a donation today by clicking the link below. __** ### _

Janoo’s full quote on tourism and the economy: “These are the major concerns I have. A lot of our rural economies and Vermont’s economy, has gone through a process where we are increasingly very dependent on tourism, on real estate, maybe some financial services... things that are **unstable and inherently kind of extractive” **_

Help us get the Governor over the finish line on November 3rd with a donation today by clicking the link below. ** To do that we must support the farms, restaurants, inns, cafes, breweries, ski areas, and recreation trails that attract visitors from across the country and around the world. Together, they provide jobs and tax revenue and create enormous economic benefits for our State. In fact, it is one of our most stable economic sectors. I saw my opponent described tourism as "extractive,” at the World’s Fair in Tunbridge... which itself creates great economic activity from out of state visitors for the region every year. ** Like me, you might wonder what “extractive” means? It’s a term some people use to describe when resources are taken from a community, without economic value being returned. Now, I see it differently, because tourism in Vermont supports hundreds of small businesses, employs tens of thousands of Vermonters, and helps rural communities across our state. In 2024, for example, visitors: Spent $4.2 BILLION at Vermont businesses; Supported nearly 32,000 JOBS ; and Generated an estimated $293.5 MILLION in state and local taxes. I’ve spent decades listening to Vermont’s employers, supporting our hospitality and recreation sectors, and working to make Vermont a place where more people can afford to live, work, raise a family, and retire. Vermont’s future depends on GROWING our economy, not dismissing entire sectors that help make economic growth possible in every part of Vermont. And in the campaign for governor the choice could not be clearer. That’s something to know before you vote. Oh, and one more thing... if not for tourism, and Tom Watson’s love for our ski mountains, IBM would not have been built in Vermont... think about that. Thanks - Gov. Hey folks,
The Trump White House is turning into Game of Thrones, and everybody has a knife.
Katie Zacharia is out after a spectacularly chaotic run as press secretary, but the bigger story is how it happened. New reporting points to Susie Wiles asserting her power after Trump reportedly hired Zacharia behind her back. Now Trump's own inner circle is fighting for control while the midterms get closer.
* [**00:01:00**] We break down the reporting that Trump hired Katie Zacharia without telling Susie Wiles--and why that decision set this entire disaster in motion.
* [**00:04:17**] Sean Hannity grills Zacharia over her credentials in an extraordinary Fox News interview, and I explain why I don't think that happens without someone powerful giving the green light.
* [**00:06:55**] Susie Wiles appears to remind Trump exactly how much power she has inside MAGA, and why getting rid of her might be harder than he thinks.
* [**00:09:28**] Wiles and Natalie Harp emerge all smiles after Zacharia's exit while Trump's inner circle increasingly looks like a collection of rival factions fighting each other.
* [**00:12:07**] Zacharia is officially out, Scott Jennings suddenly has an opening, and we zoom out to what all this chaos could mean with Republicans staring down a brutal midterm environment.

This isn't just funny White House gossip. It's a window into an administration increasingly consumed by loyalty tests, internal power struggles, incompetence, and corruption instead of making people's lives better. name: Brian Lenney
subject: The Tale of the Two Sisters
body:

| |
---|---|---
|
# The Tale of the Two Sisters
### One in Idaho. One in California.
| | | [Brian Lenney](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
| Oct 19
---
| [](https://substack.com/@brianlenney)
---
Picture two sisters walking into two different abortion clinics on the same morning...
One's in Sacramento. The other's in Boise.
They're twins, and they got pregnant around the same time. Both are 23 weeks along. And the mom and baby are healthy in both cases with no emergency or complications.
Neither one wants the baby.
So each doctor has to answer the same question:
_**If this baby were born today, could he survive?**_
The best numbers we have come from a big NIH study of preemies. Of babies born at 23 weeks, about one in three made it (33%). It's better today at the best NICUs.
Now the law.
In California, a baby is protected once there's a _" reasonable likelihood"_ he'd survive outside the womb. After that, abortion is only allowed if the mom's life or health is at risk.
That means the Sacramento doctor looks at a one out of three shot at surviving and asks whether that's a _" reasonable"_ chance. Plenty of doctors would say yes. The baby's viable and the mom's healthy.
So, no abortion.
**The sister in Sacramento goes home** _**still pregnant.**_
But in Idaho, if Prop 1 passes, the bar moves.
The lefties pushing this (a group ironically called _Idahoans United for Women and Families_) copied California's definition almost word for word. Then they changed one word. _" Reasonable"_ became _" significant."_
The Boise doctor (or "provider," because under Prop 1 it doesn't have to be a doctor) asks a different question...
Is a one in three shot at surviving _" significant"_?
That's a "no" for most abortion providers because nobody calls something that fails two out of three times "significant." So the baby's not viable and Prop 1 lets her get the abortion _for any reason._
**The sister in Boise walks out** _**not pregnant.**_
California would've protected him.
Idaho under Prop 1 would not.
Most people in Idaho have no clue this is in there. Idahoans United for Women and Families campaign ads talk about medical emergencies, but neither of these sisters had one.
This is why we have to shut this down.
[Here's a slide deck I made on this recently](https://substack.com/redirect/a9c95505-3f3a-4fab-9d18-b4eeb53d19f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) »
Let me know if you have any questions.
Cheers,
Brian
**P.S.** Prop 1 gives this right to "every person." Not every adult. Your daughter can't get a Tylenol from the school nurse without your permission. Prop 1 could make abortion the exception.
**P.P.S.** Early voting is open now in a lot of Idaho counties, and Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3. Forward this to somebody who hasn't been paying attention. They're the ones who'll decide this.
(C) 2026 Brian Lenney

You’re invited to tonight’s Take Back The House virtual phone bank with Red-to-Blue candidate for CA-22 Randy Villegas!

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/derektranforcongress/2026-oct-19-phone-bank-blast?e=fa48019594)
---
| | | | |

| | Dear Supporter,
You’re invited to tonight’s _**Take Back The House**_ virtual phone bank with Red-to-Blue candidate for CA-22 Randy Villegas!
**WHEN:** Monday, October 19 5 - 7 p.m. PT**WHERE:** Virtual**RSVP:**[**HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/WkVqyBs4md3?e=fa48019594&c2id=2d2f4814b3c86de5c7569386ec1a86b4)
To receive your virtual meeting link, training to call voters in both CA-45 and CA-22, and hear from us on our plan to take back the House, please RSVP via the link above. I hope to see you there!
Sincerely,Congressman Derek Tran
---
| | ###
_The son of refugees who worked hard and sacrificed for the American Dream, Congressman Derek Tran joined the Army at 18 to give back to the country that has given him so much. Wanting to continue his career in public service, he ran in California's 45th district to put people ahead of politics and protect democracy, and won. Now, he's running again to ensure everyone no matter what neighborhood they come from has the opportunity to succeed without fear of their freedoms being taken away._
_California’s 45th Congressional District remains one of the most contested battleground races in the country. Last cycle, Derek Tran flipped the seat by just over 600 votes (a 0.2% margin) in the second-closest and most expensive House race ($46 million spent) in the country. A majority-minority district, the District has the third largest AAPI population (41%) of any Congressional District, is 28% Latino, and is home to the largest Vietnamese community in the country. Following Proposition 50, this district brings in over 15,000 new Hispanic voters and over 7,000 new Vietnamese voters, and has a DPI of 52.8%. It includes all or part of the cities of Garden Grove, Westminster, Fountain Valley, Cerritos, Buena Park, Placentia, Hawaiian Gardens, Cypress, Artesia, Los Alamitos, La Palma, Norwalk, Stanton, Lakewood, Santa Ana, Seal Beach, and Fullerton, as well as the unincorporated community of Midway City._

subject: Fighting for Affordability

body:
Something I am hearing every day in California: the cost of living is crushing families here. | | |
---
| |
# Fighting for Affordability
---
| Friend, Something I am hearing every day in California: the cost of living is crushing families here. Ask anyone in our district what worries them most, and the high cost of living tops the list. I’ve been fighting for more affordability in California since my first day in Sacramento and I’ve continued that fight in Washington, DC. Back [in 2020, when I introduced legislation to cut taxes](https://us.list-manage.com/13yMt3dNpaz?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8) for middle class families, small businesses, and renters, I said plainly: _"The cost of living in California is driving out so many families to other states because they cannot bear this burden any longer."_ That same year, [I called out Sacramento](https://us.list-manage.com/4jGYZDROlMJ?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8) for quietly hiking the gas tax by another $440 million without so much as a vote of the Legislature or the public. By [2022, with inflation hammering household budgets](https://us.list-manage.com/wekW4nxiB76?e=affd398937&c2id=4fd8e839bd16eef39626cb246bcc01d8) and gas topping $5.70 a gallon in parts of our state, I was back at it again, introducing legislation to suspend the state gas tax outright. Something is wrong in California when the average price of gasoline in our state is $6.21 and the average price in Indiana is $3.89. We know one of the first things our out of state friends do while visiting is they take a photo of California’s gas prices. I've been fighting this fight since I first got to the State Assembly in 2016, long before affordability became the issue everyone's suddenly talking about. It's why I've spent my time in Congress fighting Sacramento's hidden climate tax on shipping that drives up prices at the register and the pump. It's why I fought to pull the plug on California's $128 billion high-speed rail boondoggle instead of letting it drain resources from roads and water systems that actually serve our families. It's why I'm fighting the State Water Board every time it tries to raise costs and uncertainty for the farmers who feed this country. It’s why I am working to expand oil and gas production in our community, to invest in California’s energy pipeline infrastructure, and to actually build and expand refining capacity to support increase supplies of needed gasoline, diesel and jet fuel. I will continue to work every single day to tackle the affordability crisis in California. Let’s invest in water infrastructure to increase needed water supplies for our homes, businesses and farms. Let’s increase California’s gasoline and diesel supplies to lower prices at the pump. Let’s get rid of red tape and bureaucracy that is making everything more expensive. And let’s reduce your tax burden so you keep more of your hard earned money. Thank you for standing with me,
Congressman Vince Fong

body:
The numbers look good. Here’s why I’m not taking a victory lap.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141740770/654587184/-1038038363?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_NF_Briefing2_261005_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTgzYjc2M2UtZDhjYi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=DnWC9zWvEvBmizlo7pqyE_f5UmfRnWJyMeSH6ApRwLE=&emci=e203d2a6-cccb-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=e83b763e-d8cb-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=17458827)
Peter,

I want to give you an update on what I’m seeing as chair of the Democratic Governors’ Association and in my conversations with candidates and voters as I’m traveling the country for campaign stops:

Democrats are doing well in the polls. Folks are tired of rising costs and ready for leaders who will focus on their families. I’m encouraged by that.

But I know a thing or two about tough races. I’ve won three times statewide in a state Donald Trump carried by more than 30 points, and I can tell you that a poll is a snapshot, not a result. Nobody gets a trophy for being ahead with two weeks to go. You run through the tape.

That’s why In This Together is running ads and making direct contributions to candidates in tough races. This election is absolutely critical for the future of our country, and we have to compete in as many places as possible.

Here are just a few of the things at stake:

Diesel hit an all-time high last month, and it’s still above six dollars a gallon. Gas is more than a dollar higher than it was a year ago. That’s going to raise the cost of transporting groceries, building materials and just about everything else you buy. Donald Trump’s war with Iran has driven those prices up, and working families are the ones paying for it.

Back home in Kentucky, we’re dealing with the highest number of measles cases in 35 years. Diseases we had virtually eliminated are coming back because of bad public health advice and a Secretary of Health and Human Services, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who isn’t qualified to be giving it.

And there’s something else weighing on me this week. More than 80,000 Kentuckians have lost access to SNAP benefits because of the Trump administration’s cuts, and they’re now at risk of going hungry. So last week, I sent a letter to the Trump administration asking them to take action. Nobody should have to wonder where their next meal is coming from.

My faith teaches me to love my neighbor, and everyone is my neighbor. Right now, a lot of our neighbors are getting squeezed, and they deserve leaders who show up for them.

So here’s what I’m asking of you. Make a plan to vote. Check on a neighbor who might not. Talk to the friend who’s sitting this one out. If you’ve got an hour to spare, go knock some doors for a candidate you believe in. And as always, please reply with your thoughts about this election – I’d love to hear from you.

Let’s run through the tape together.

Thank you for all you do.

Andy

As a retired general, I can tell you that the military carries out its most difficult missions with dignity, respect, and a quiet discipline that honors those who serve. Pete Hegseth thinks it's okay to turn it into a horrific reality TV show, and that's downright disgraceful--and it says more than he might realize about his ability to do his job. Take this _New York Times_ headline.

clean_body: | | Pete Hegseth's proposed livestream of an execution may have been shut down after righteous backlash sounded from around the country. As a retired general, I can tell you that the military carries out its most difficult missions with dignity, respect, and a quiet discipline that honors those who serve. Pete Hegseth thinks it's okay to turn it into a horrific reality TV show, and that's downright disgraceful--and it says more than he might realize about his ability to do his job. Take this New York Times headline. | As the article goes on to say: " Men with real accomplishments on the battlefield don't tend to talk this way." After 40 years in uniform, I couldn't agree more. This job is simply too big for Pete Hegseth to handle. Discipline, judgment, and accountability are not optional in military leadership. Hegseth has shown none of them. His amateurism is endangering our troops and making America less safe. He needs to be fired -- and Clay Fuller can't be trusted to do it. Our troops deserve far better from their leader, and they deserve far better from the members of Congress who refuse to hold that leader accountable. It's time to send someone to Congress who will stand up for our troops even when it's not politically convenient -- someone who will demand more from leadership and take real action to make it happen. ~~ ~~ Thank you, Ret. Join us for a community call and start organizing! | | | Peter, This administration’s mass delegalization agenda didn’t slow down. It just got harder to see. In July, federal immigration agents made nearly 51,000 arrests, a record high. And they're doing it faster and quieter than ever. People are being detained while taking out the trash, pumping gas, driving to work, and at the airport. [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMchKqTlnDL9HV9V-hz_r8qN5sFN7uyIDHDQ_kqfTbgHpw9l-ngjXclNoM0Ou8ZiAaIE1OF_xDI2niJbM2MS9qEr46VmGhJKSYFLbW3lXcl5FUJw1q1QM1mIj3xmkRXtB3M9TSvHNFHC-xHvrULAcvX2z2e1i8p7CeeO_-TjYYp_T9Os0dmRzaZSBoYtKPR6mKeYbVBGpUUsv0zpiIs-PJ7IvLK_JYIRNlZxQBFaXXzvIdpegoGkb43YRLze_uA0RP-qMLwenP7apxnCZOZagejED0V47IWag2blF3KiFKSs4/4v0/C9Y5ovkxTZyBeybhus5pyQ/h0/h001.pURnbE2pPSaU-NDl3SR0j3XWgXx03ReraSIG8ODM7_Q) It’s not just federal agents anymore. Families are being torn apart, and people are being kept in detention; permanent citizenship is the only solution.

**********CHAPPAQUA, NY –** Cait Conley, Army combat veteran and Democratic nominee for New York’s 17th Congressional District, was joined yesterday by the Westchester Jewish Democrats, the Jewish Democratic Council of America, and local leaders for a rally in support of the Jewish community, followed by a canvass launch. Speakers emphasized the importance of fighting back against antisemitism in all its forms and highlighted Cait Conley as the candidate who will best support and defend the Jewish community — here in the Hudson Valley and across the country. “As antisemitism rises at alarming rates in New York and across the country, today is about standing in solidarity with our Jewish neighbors, and demonstrating that hate has no place in the Hudson Valley. It is incumbent upon all of us — especially our elected leaders — to fight back against antisemitism in all its forms and never fuel it. I will always be committed to ensuring that our Jewish community members feel safe and welcome here, and I’m incredibly grateful for the support of groups like the Westchester Jewish Democrats and the Jewish Democratic Council of America, ” said **Cait Conley, Democratic nominee for New York’s 17th Congressional District.** “To have a candidate during these times we know we can count on to stand strong with our community is incredible. It is so important right now for Jewish Democrats broadly, and certainly here in NY-17. Let’s go out and get this done for Cait Conley,” said **Nancy Street, Chair of the Westchester Jewish Democrats.** “NY-17 has the largest Jewish voting population of any of the vitally important red-to-blue congressional districts in the country, with Jewish Americans making up nearly one-fifth of its population. We're proud to support veteran Cait Conley in this race, and are confident a majority of Jewish voters in the district will vote for her because she aligns with our values,” said **Halie Soifer, CEO of the Jewish Democratic Council of America.** **** **** ### **About Cait Conley** Cait Conley is a Hudson Valley native, the daughter of a postal worker and a construction worker. She applied to West Point the day after 9/11 and went on to serve in the Army, first as a military police officer and then in special operations leadership, deploying six times and earning three Bronze Stars. Cait concluded her active-duty career as Director for Counterterrorism at the National Security Council, where Russia sanctioned her for her work, and then served as a senior executive at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, protecting critical infrastructure and the systems that run our elections. She put her life on the line to serve this country, not any person or political party, and especially not corporate special interests. Now, Cait is running to take on corruption so politicians can’t keep lining their pockets at the taxpayers’ expense, including by banning stock trading; lowering middle-class taxes; and holding monopoly utility companies and Big Pharma accountable to lower costs. To learn more, visit [caitconley.com](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.BMyXzJRPwu_AnDhWGQjUxHaFuvXbS1BlNO-Lh096nHqNeLz6rAAezYwB5jy2M8I9mctsSdX5b_CkHeHCJ1mFDf1HqPr3HgVxdyEtGMd4wY5A5EyDcaAmJaNM_z1GWWjqYZfoc0wpdRNp4rolO45TRU1TvcWqc4Iceh_CnK_egBwnW1sVBMhyfTorcudU8ertHyX6AyHs7B5Roxg5PmzCRFM6m1yCpa7mZuYj_4dQJQgDy9Pvh_gt-G5AJc00_GQIcdyw07nTdIqM4lmmiJxGhjLlVvzPW1WM7iX5qyPXB3RUqlu2EZbZLRiL3dunNw2LtZ9bt_GqOoChb2u_719KWXuq1cOa3Lz8y8L_twvrZkZq9a1jqZbRsyuWeRt0IE-JWwtWZods6YZp5sx6LGliBA/4v0/Z0_WfFVDRDCsuKHwC3JSJQ/h2/h001.1vwVjsIa4dt5XAnQLCwID_3D6SDmbuZG5UQAEFf06AI).

If we’re caught flat-footed tomorrow, we could jeopardize our chances of flipping this seat.

Peter, we’re running out of time.
**President Trump is coming to North Carolina tomorrow** for his big MAGA rally with my opponent, Michael Whatley, and we need to hit our $1,000,000 goal before then. We can’t get there without grassroots support from people like you. [**_Please, will you chip in $5 or any amount right now to help us close the gap?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1702&amount=5&t=8&akid=4739%2E124072%2Ege4NqY)
I want to share three reasons why your $5 will make a huge difference for our campaign.
1\. If we lose in NC, Democrats lose our shot at taking back the Senate for the people. That’s why the GOP – including Trump’s own super PAC – has poured millions into this race to defeat me.
2\. In our state, winning a U.S. Senate race by a “landslide” means winning, at best, 51% of the vote and we haven’t elected a Democrat in almost two decades. That’s how competitive our elections are, no matter what the polls or pundits say.
3\. We’re falling short of our $1 million goal to respond to Trump’s oncoming attacks. If we’re caught flat-footed tomorrow, we could jeopardize our chances of flipping this seat.
Unlike Whatley, I don’t rely on megadonors to swoop in and save our campaign when we fall short. I fully depend on people like _you_ , Peter, chipping in what you can, when you can to power this grassroots movement forward.
**Right now, I need you with me.[_Will you please give $5 to help us close the gap on our crucial goal before Trump comes to North Carolina? It’s the only way we can keep up our momentum, win this race and take back the Senate._](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1702&amount=5&t=9&akid=4739%2E124072%2Ege4NqY)**

Your Next Vehicle Might Charge in Your Garage and Take Off From Your Driveway.
This summer, new FAA rules opened a path for small personal electric aircraft to be certified for the first time. A handful of companies are racing to build them, and some are letting ordinary investors buy in before any public listing. It’s early, it’s risky, and it’s exactly the stage when new industries are born.

The car changed where Americans could live and work. The garage became the most important room in the suburban house. Now some engineers believe the next vehicle to sit in that garage won’t have wheels at all. It will plug in overnight like an electric car, and in the morning, it will lift straight up.
The evidence board
| | Why This Is Suddenly Realistic
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the rulebook.** On July 24, 2026, the aircraft part of the FAA’s modernized light-sport rules took effect, making small, personally owned electric vertical-takeoff aircraft eligible for the category for the first time.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the demand.** According to INRIX, the typical U.S. driver lost 49 hours to traffic in 2025. In Chicago, it was 112 hours.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the access.** Under the SEC’s Regulation A, private companies can raise money directly from everyday investors, not just venture funds, long before they list on an exchange.
| CHATTER
---
This isn’t easy. German air-taxi developer Lilium went insolvent in 2024 after burning through its funding. Certification is long and expensive, and not every company will make it. That risk is exactly why the early price can be so low.
| OUR THEORY
---
For decades, the only people who could invest in a new transportation industry at the start were venture capitalists. By the time the public could buy shares, the biggest gains were often gone. Personal flight may be one of the first new industries where ordinary investors can get in on the ground floor.

When more of your life plugs into the wall, having power when the grid fails matters more than ever.
